$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60: Stanley Kubrick only. Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1); extra optional fields: films[].flags, nearMisses[].imdb/rt. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the roster, the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Eligibility (sole or credited TMDB Directing credit, feature or, where flagged, feature-length documentary) -> longlist with evidence panel -> tier by directing achievement (craft, innovation, influence, canon) with IMDb and RT used only as within-source ordinal sanity checks -> order within tier by documented editorial judgement. IMDb /10 and Tomatometer % are never averaged or combined.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (ratings and vote counts); title.basics and title.crew used to match ids and confirm sole directors
imdb.note: Dataset file run-date 2026-11-12, last-modified 2026-11-13 00:28 GMT. The live IMDb title page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool on 2026-11-13, so ratings were not cross-checked against live pages. Dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see SCORE_SOURCING_NOTES.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer percentage and its critic review count
rt.note: Read through a text-extraction fetch tool, one film page at a time. Percentages were cross-checked against the RT celebrity filmography table where it listed them and, for some films, against search-result summaries of the same page. Review counts are live and change daily; each is a single dated read.

films.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Made the science-fiction film a vehicle for pure image and music, with almost no dialogue, a staged sense of scale and a vision of technology that still sets the terms for the genre; it carries the strongest combined evidence in his filmography.

films.title: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
films.originalTitle: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A Cold War nuclear-crisis thriller turned into black comedy, built from three rigorously separated spaces (war room, bomber, base) and a multi-role performance by Peter Sellers; the highest Tomatometer of his major films.

films.title: A Clockwork Orange
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A violent satire of state and individual control whose visual design, ironic use of classical music and rigidly composed wide-angle images made it one of the most imitated and argued-over films of its decade; ranked above The Shining on influence even though the audience score is a little lower.

films.title: The Shining
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Early extended use of the Steadicam turns a hotel into a maze of unstable space and a horror film into a study of a family under pressure; first on IMDb among his films, lowest of the top five on the Tomatometer, a gap this ranking treats as a settled dispute about genre, not about craft.

films.title: Paths of Glory
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: First-World-War court-martial drama with long tracking shots through the trenches and a mercilessly clear structure; the film that established him as a major director and still scores near the top on both evidence lines.

films.title: Barry Lyndon
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Eighteenth-century picaresque shot largely by natural and candle light with very fast lenses; the film that most clearly shows his command of period image-making.

films.title: Full Metal Jacket
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A two-part war film (boot camp, then Vietnam) that reads as a study of how violence is trained and then released; strong on both evidence lines.

films.title: The Killing
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Heist thriller told out of sequence from several viewpoints; the first fully realised Kubrick film and a formal model for later crime cinema.

films.title: Spartacus
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A large-scale epic directed after Kubrick replaced the original director and over which he had little creative control; included for the strength of the staging, the ensemble and the evidence, and flagged as the least personal film in the ten.

films.title: Eyes Wide Shut
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: His final film: a slow, dreamlike study of jealousy and desire in a stylised New York; the closest call in the ten (see below).

nearMisses.title: Lolita
nearMisses.reason: Strong adaptation with an uneven tone; ranked just behind Eyes Wide Shut on audience standing and narrower influence.

nearMisses.title: Killer's Kiss
nearMisses.reason: Short, early noir that matters mainly as a step toward The Killing.

nearMisses.title: Fear and Desire
nearMisses.reason: First feature, later withdrawn by Kubrick himself; historical interest only.

unverified: TMDB film ids and Directing credits were read from the TMDB person page on 2026-11-13 (no TMDB API key was available), not from the API crew.job field; title-to-id pairs were taken from the page links. Co-director status was checked against the IMDb dataset crew file (title.crew), which lists a sole director for every film in the list.
IMDb ids were matched in the IMDb dataset by original title, year and runtime, not read from a TMDB external_ids field; confirm with the TMDB API external_ids at implementation.
RT review counts are a single read on the stated date via a text fetcher.
IMDb title pages could not be read (HTTP 403); ratings and votes come from the official dataset (not cross-checked against the live pages), whose licence is non-commercial only.
TMDB person-page years displayed by the fetch tool were sometimes offset for other directors; for Kubrick all years match the original release years used here.
